source.title: Practical Guide to the International Alignment of Research Data Management — Extended Edition

requirements.section: Data description and collection or re-use of existing data
requirements.question: How will new data be collected or produced and/or how will existing data be re-used?
requiredTopics: methodologies or software used to collect or produce new data
constraints on re-use of existing data
reasons for discarding existing data sources considered for re-use

facts.gap: The KM captures instrument datasets and instruments but has no general field for methodology or software.

requirements.section: Data description and collection or re-use of existing data
requirements.question: What data (for example the kinds, formats, and volumes) will be collected or produced?
requiredTopics: format rationale and preference for open standards

requirements.question: What metadata and documentation (for example the methodology of data collection and way of organising data) will accompany the data?
What data quality control measures will be used?

requirements.section: Storage and backup during the research process
requirements.question: How will data and metadata be stored and backed up during the research process?
requiredTopics: robust managed storage and automatic backup

facts.gap: The answers describe responsibility or strategy but not a complete backup schedule.
No directly mapped answer states the primary and backup locations.
No directly mapped answer states backup frequency.

requirements.section: Storage and backup during the research process
requirements.question: How will data security and protection of sensitive data be taken care of during the research?

requirements.section: Legal and ethical requirements, codes of conduct
requirements.question: If personal data are processed, how will compliance with legislation on personal data and on security be ensured?

requirements.section: Legal and ethical requirements, codes of conduct
requirements.question: How will other legal issues, such as intellectual property rights and ownership, be managed? What legislation is applicable?

requirements.section: Legal and ethical requirements, codes of conduct
requirements.question: What ethical issues and codes of conduct are there, and how will they be taken into account?
requiredTopics: ethical effects on storage, transfer, access, and retention

requirements.question: How and when will data be shared? Are there possible restrictions to data sharing or embargo reasons?
How will data for preservation be selected, and where will data be preserved long-term (for example a data repository or archive)?
requiredTopics: legal or contractual retention and destruction
repository policies, procedures, standards, and costs

requirements.question: What methods or software tools are needed to access and use data?
requiredTopics: special tools needed for access or re-use

requirements.question: How will the application of a unique and persistent identifier (such as a Digital Object Identifier (DOI)) to each data set be ensured?
Who (for example role, position, and institution) will be responsible for data management (i.e. the data steward)?
requiredTopics: roles and named responsibilities across the data lifecycle

requirements.question: What resources (for example financial and time) will be dedicated to data management and ensuring that data will be FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Re-usable)?
requiredTopics: costed time and resources for curation, sharing, and preservation
storage, hardware, staff, deposit, and repository costs
amount and source of cost coverage

facts.gap: Cost items can include staff time and other resources, but completeness depends on free-text descriptions and project cost entries.
